A1.justification: Both PDFs describe INDIEVALUECATALOG and INDIEVALUEREASONER. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model evaluations, reasoner-training experiments, ablations, and demographic analyses in Sections 3–4 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds restricted-pool baseline results and a continental response-evenness analysis.

M1.justification: The Llama-3.1-8B fine-tuning procedure, statement-prediction task, and polar/refined and mixed-demonstration configurations remain unchanged. Expanded explanations do not establish a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same WVS-derived coverage: 93,279 respondents, 253 value questions, 31 demographic questions, and the retained continental and demographic evaluations. The added analyses reuse these data.

E2.justification: v2 Tables 3 and 18 add Resemble (1600, top 1) and Resemble (1600, top cluster) comparator variants. The original full-pool Resemble baselines are retained with 'all' labels, alongside the same language-model comparators.

E3.justification: v2 adds comparisons restricting the Resemble reference pool to 1,600 randomly sampled individuals and introduces Shannon evenness for continental data analysis. The original 800-person evaluation set, three 39-question probing splits, decoding settings, and training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new Shannon-evenness analysis tests the earlier hypothesis that Oceania responses are unusually homogeneous. The restricted-pool comparisons further examine sample efficiency. Conversely, the detailed Llama/reasoner income and social-class subgroup panels disappear; their aggregate inequity scores remain in Table 19.

E5.justification: Three-split averaging and the existing distributional boxplots are retained. v2 adds no seed or repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or specified significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: New overall accuracies are 56.60 for Resemble (1600, top 1) and 62.38 for its top-cluster variant; Figure 7 adds evenness results, including Oceania's 0.769. The best reasoner remains at 67.67. However, v2 Table 3 reports 58.27 for the refined p+r/mixed/N=800 result, versus 59.40 in both v1 Table 4 and v2 Table 18. Detailed income/social-class subgroup plot results are also omitted.

T1.justification: The task, accuracy, and Value Inequity Index definitions remain substantively unchanged. The added standard Shannon-evenness formula explains an empirical metric; it introduces no new theoretical result, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain individualistic alignment, the WVS-derived dataset, limited frontier-model proficiency, demographic inequity, and improved reasoning through fine-tuning. Abstract and conclusion compression does not materially change these claims across the paper.

C2.justification: v2 presents Oceania's lower diversity as quantitatively supported and adds specific limitations concerning single-prompt evaluation and simplification through statement conversion. It also discusses potential applications and alternative data-processing choices. Its new claim that training was limited to 200 individuals per question conflicts with the larger configurations retained in Section 4.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly describes WVS research-use licensing and non-redistribution restrictions. The repository resource, prompts, hyperparameters, eight-H100 hardware configuration, and reported training time remain substantively unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds CulturalBench and references connecting the work to social simulation and computational social science: Park et al., Zhou et al., and Ziems et al. It removes background references including Ahmadian, Carroll, Ganguli, Ge, and Lin. The main positioning relative to pluralistic alignment and personalization remains intact.

P1.justification: Much of the main text is condensed and rewritten, with declarative result headings replacing questions. Related Work becomes a separate section, philosophical background moves to Appendix A, and standalone Limitations and AI-assistance disclosures are added. Author affiliations and acknowledgements also change.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout and extensively resizes and relocates displays. It introduces condensed main Table 3 while retaining detailed results in Appendix Table 18, adds the evenness chart, and reduces the three-panel demographic comparison to a continent-only figure. Figure 1 corrects the reversed life-satisfaction labels; this alone does not establish that preprocessing or experiments changed.

improvement.justification: The 1,600-person comparison controls strengthen the sample-efficiency argument, and the evenness analysis provides evidence for the earlier Oceania hypothesis. Correcting Figure 1 and disclosing licensing and prompt limitations also improve clarity. These gains are limited by the new Table 3 score inconsistency, the contradictory 200-person training-limit statement, and the loss of detailed income/social-class plots. The net improvement is modest.
